8. ALTERNATIVES TO THE PROPOSED ACTION
Tables 8-2 through 8-4 present tabular comparisons between the proposed project and reasonable alternatives. The tables compare capital costs, production costs, system fuel consumption, transmission line lengths, and quantities of atmospheric pollutants which would be produced by the operation of the proposed project and the alternatives.
8.1 NEED FOR PROJECT POWER
Table 8-1 is Applicant's scheduled capability and forecasted summer peak loads for the period 1976 to 1984, including corresponding reserve margins with and without the proposed Bad Creek Project. Table 8-1 shows that, without the Bad Creek Project, reserve margins beyond year 1982 are substantially below the 18-22 percent reserve margin recommended by the Southern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) for reliable system operation (Anon, 1975).
The pumping function of the Bad Creek Project would be accomplished by using off-peak generation from base-load nuclear and/or high efficiency fossil-fueled units. During on-peak hours, water would be released to generate power and displace Applicant's low efficiency, intermediate operation, coal-fired, cycling units. As shown in Tables 8-2 through 8-3, substantial reductions in Applicant's production costs and fossil fuel consumption would be realized.
During the first 2 years of project operation, the major portion of the pumping energy would probably be provided from the large coal-fired Marshall and Balews Creek units. Thereafter, most of the off-peak pumping energy would be provided from low production-cost nuclear units.
